headline: Tailors on bikes, cookies with a reverse age check and a funeral for an alibi

campaigns.summary: Tailors on bicycles will visit residents at home to repair, alter and refresh clothes free of charge during Black Week.
campaigns.did: For Black Week, the City of Gothenburg is offering Hemlagat: tailors on bicycles who will visit residents at home to repair, alter and refresh clothes free of charge. Visits are planned for 23 to 29 November and are booked on the city's website. The tailors resemble food delivery couriers, and the name means home-cooked but also splits into the Swedish words for home and repaired.
campaigns.why: It answers a week of offers with a counter-offer that costs nothing and takes the effort out of repair. Dagens PS and Metro Mode report that 15 local tailors are also giving discounts during the week. No results are out yet, as the visits have not started.
campaigns.steal: When everyone else is discounting, offer a free service that makes the alternative to buying easier. Borrow a format people already know, here the delivery courier, so the idea needs no explaining.

campaigns.summary: A limited-edition cookie pack for gamers too young for the 18+ game GTA VI, with a QR code that opens a private Discord community.
campaigns.did: ChipsMore! made 18 Unrestricted, a limited-edition cookie pack for gamers too young for the 18+ game GTA VI. A QR code behind the label opens a private Discord community where Malaysian gaming personalities are set to share tips for games such as Mobile Legends: Bang Bang and PUBG Mobile. The packs are to be sold at booths in Lotus's stores, where bouncers will check MyKad identity documents.
campaigns.why: Most brands chased the adults playing on launch day. This one picked the audience left out and turned the age check, usually a barrier, into the reward. No results are out yet, and ContentGrip notes that any effect on store traffic is unreported.
campaigns.steal: Look at who a big cultural moment excludes and build something only they can get. Reversing a familiar gate, so the usual outsiders are the ones let in, gives people a story to retell.

campaigns.summary: A funeral for a fictional character on the day GTA VI launches, to give gamers a reason to be away from work.
campaigns.did: KFC announced a funeral for a fictional character, Ann Alibi, at its Robina restaurant on the Gold Coast at 11am on 19 November, the day GTA VI launches. The idea is to give gamers a reason to be away from work. Plans included a book of condolences, an order of service, proof of attendance and free chicken, with an Instagram livestream and free app delivery on orders over $30 for those at home.
campaigns.why: A pun became a full event with an offer attached, and KFC says plainly that attending does not guarantee compassionate leave. Mediaweek, Dexerto and Campaign Brief all covered it before the day. No attendance or sales figures are out yet.
campaigns.steal: Find the excuse your audience is already looking for and stage it for real. Pair a physical moment for the few with a stream and an offer for everyone else.
